title: Query Deconstruction / Expansion
summary: Turn complex or underspecified questions into bounded retrieval plans while preserving the original intent and evidence requirements.
overview: Query deconstruction separates a compound question into answerable subquestions. Query expansion adds useful synonyms, abbreviations, or alternative phrasing to improve recall. They solve different problems: decomposition organizes dependencies, while expansion broadens the wording used to search. Both should remain traceable to the original request.

Unconstrained rewriting can change a date, erase a negation, invent an entity, or multiply searches without improving evidence. A retrieval planner should preserve hard constraints, cap fan-out, and distinguish exploratory terms from factual premises. The final answer must reconcile sub-results rather than concatenate potentially conflicting fragments.

production.poc: A prototype logs original questions and rewrites so an evaluator can identify intent drift.
production.production: Production validates entities and constraints, caps subqueries, and tracks which evidence answers each original requirement.
production.scale: At scale, cache safe expansions, allocate retrieval budgets by uncertainty, and evaluate multi-hop questions separately from simple lookups.

components.name: Intent parser
components.role: Extracts entities, dates, comparison dimensions, and hard constraints.

components.name: Retrieval planner
components.role: Chooses decomposition, expansion, or an unchanged query.

components.name: Budget controller
components.role: Caps subqueries, parallelism, and total retrieval cost.

components.name: Evidence matrix
components.role: Maps each requirement to retrieved supporting or conflicting passages.

components.name: Synthesis validator
components.role: Checks that the final response covers the original question without unsupported bridging claims.

flow.title: Extract constraints
flow.description: Identify exact names, time periods, exclusions, and requested comparisons.

flow.title: Choose transformation
flow.description: Decompose only when separate evidence needs exist; expand terminology when wording is the main obstacle.

flow.title: Validate subqueries
flow.description: Check that each query retains relevant constraints and contributes a distinct evidence objective.

flow.title: Retrieve within budget
flow.description: Run independent queries in parallel and dependent queries only after needed entities resolve.

flow.title: Reconcile evidence
flow.description: Deduplicate passages and record missing or contradictory support by requirement.

flow.title: Answer the original task
flow.description: Synthesize against the initial question and disclose unresolved portions explicitly.

useCase.title: Comparing regional retention rules
useCase.situation: A records team asks how two approved regional policies differ for the same document class.
useCase.problem: One broad query retrieves general policy summaries but misses exceptions and effective dates.
useCase.requirement: Build a comparison with separate support for each region and exception.
useCase.architecture: A planner creates bounded region-specific queries and an evidence matrix keyed by retention, exceptions, and date.
runtime: The system retrieves each region’s active policy and exception section.
A validator refuses to fill a missing comparison cell with a plausible model assumption.
useCase.failure: If a rewrite changes the document class, constraint validation rejects it before retrieval.
useCase.impact: Measure requirement coverage, rewrite drift, and search fan-out; more queries are useful only when they close identifiable evidence gaps.

tradeoffs.cost: Increase irrelevant candidates and retrieval cost.
Adds planning latency and reconciliation complexity.
Can create burst load and redundant searches.

failures.detection: Subquery semantics conflict with the original exclusion.
failures.recovery: Preserve hard constraints in structured fields and reject the rewrite.

failures.detection: Search results follow an unsupported name.
failures.recovery: Validate entity references against the request or retrieved evidence.

mistakes.fix: Use transformation only when evaluation shows benefit.
Set depth, subquery, and token budgets.
Reconcile sources and effective dates before synthesis.

whenToUse: Use for comparisons and multi-part evidence questions.
Use when domain abbreviations reduce lexical recall.
Use when retrieval misses can be traced to query wording.
whenNotToUse: Avoid transformations for exact identifiers already retrieving correctly.
Do not let expansion modify authorization scope.
Avoid decomposing inseparable mathematical or causal claims into unsupported pieces.
checklist: Evaluate intent drift and coverage together.
